elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 7.6 reads: "Customer shall pay no liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." This is an unconditional, Agreement-wide statement that replaces the prior USD 25,000/day liquidated damages charge, leaving no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The redline eliminates all Customer-payable liquidated amounts rather than framing one as an early-termination fee; no early-termination fee is created, so this fallback element is not implemented (the preferred level is taken instead).

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee exists in the rendered language, and no three-month cap appears; the cap is only mentioned in the margin comment as a possible concession, which is not operative.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: No sole-liquidated-amount formulation appears; the clause instead negates all liquidated amounts, so the fallback checklist as written is not satisfied.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is met by the unconditional replacement of § 7.6 with "Customer shall pay no liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." The prohibition is not conditioned on any trigger and no residual per-day accrual, minimum fee, or contingent payment mechanic survives.

Fallback level is incomplete (all three elements unmet), but that is immaterial because completeness is required at only one level; the drafter correctly elected the preferred position and merely offered the fallback in the comment.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to the single offending sentence in § 7.6, adds no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no procedure, and no requirement outside the LD checklist. No favourable Customer-side language elsewhere was deleted or paraphrased.

Intent preserved: Vendor's ordinary remedies for Customer delay (damages, suspension, termination for breach) are untouched, no cross-reference to § 7.6 is left dangling, no defined term is orphaned, and no retained sentence contradicts the new statement.

Note for the drafter: the replacement sentence is scoped "under this Agreement," which is appropriate and broader than § 7.6 alone; if any Order Form or SOW template could later introduce a Customer-payable liquidated amount, confirm that Order Form terms are subordinate to the Agreement so the prohibition cannot be overridden.
